---
title: "Criterion-specific expected-error budgets"
subtitle: "4.7 · after the postrank theory book, ch. 13"
description: "Feasible report families under bounds on criterion-specific expected error shares."
---

An error weight determines the contribution of a wrong direction to risk. An error budget instead restricts its
expected share among stated directions on a specified criterion. The cloud plots allowed reports with positive
disclosure according to their two criterion-specific error shares. Applying one or both budgets reduces the feasible
family. The selected report minimises weighted risk over this remaining family, and is compared with the
unconstrained optimum under the same settings. Count-form checks also cover the all-withheld report when it is
allowed, despite its undefined error share.

```{=html}
<div id="app" class="prx-app column-page"></div>
<script src="../../js/vendor/d3.min.js"></script>
<script src="../../js/vendor/plot.min.js"></script>
<script src="../../js/bundles/error-budgets.js"></script>
<script>window.__prxApp = PRX["error-budgets"].mountWidget(document.getElementById("app"));</script>
```

## Numerical illustrations {#what-to-try}

- **Loose budget.** With equal weights and score B's budget at .03, only 3 reports qualify. The best still states
  9 of 15 pairs and has risk .0933: removing reports need not change the optimum.
- **Tight budget.** At .02, 2 reports qualify. The best states 8 of 15 pairs and has risk .0939; the other report
  withholds every comparison. The ring marks the optimum in the reduced family.
- **Exactly three.** Keeping the .02 budget while requiring exactly three grades leaves 0 reports feasible.
  The empty family has no best report. Relaxing the grade count restores the all-withheld option.
- **Both budgets.** Requiring an expected wrong share at most .02 on each score also leaves 2 reports. Both count-form checks and their slacks are reported; a report must pass both rows.
- **Zero weight.** Score B has zero error weight but still has its .10 budget. The best feasible report has risk
  .0906. Its largest single score-B error is .240, for E above F, while its average is .0267. A budget on an
  average allows some individual errors above it.
- **No budget.** The score-A-only best has risk .0417 and expected wrong share .237 on score B. The cross marks
  this unconstrained best; the older **At most .15**, **At most .10** and **At most .05** presets retain the same
  score-A-only comparison.

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
These are six fictional sites with independent normal posteriors supplied for illustration. The guarantee is an
expectation under that posterior, not the realised share of wrong directions. All-withheld has zero expected wrong
count and zero stated pairs: it meets count-form budgets when allowed, although its wrong share is undefined.
Changing weights or τ changes the loss; changing the grade cap changes the family. The browser enumerates the
six-site reports directly. postrank's typed-coefficient interface does not accept these budget settings.
:::

Standalone: [Criterion-specific expected-error budgets](../../embed/error-budgets.html), for example `?preset=both&theme=dark`.
